content:
What you did is part of the troubleshooting process, but it only fixes one possible problem, which is, if Thunderbird's interface were to crash but the program keeps running invisibly in the background. Rebooting the computer should also fix it.

Another thing that can cause this kind of condition and error message is of there is a "lock file" present when you try to start Thunderbird. A lock file is simply a small file that is created inside your Profile that will prevent you from starting a second instance of the program while one is already running, This is to prevent your email data from becoming corrupt.

Sometimes that file can be left behind if Thunderbird is not closed cleanly. If you are confident that there really are no other instances of it running, that file can safely be deleted. This article talks about the situation in more detail and explains how to remove the file

Profile in use https://kb.mozillazine.org/Profile_in_use#Remove_the_profile_lock_file

content:
I have spent a LOT of time trying to chase this down.

Here’s more information about my setup. I have Windows 11 and Thunderbird 160.0. Thunderbird.exe and related app files are installed on drive d: since c: is fairly full. The appdata folder is at C:\Users\[username]\AppData\Roaming\Thunderbird\. The profile I have used for several years, and wish to use now, is on a NAS at H:\Thunderbird profiles\Rob\Profiles.

Here are the contents of C:\Users\[username]\AppData\Roaming\Thunderbird\profiles.ini:

[General] StartWithLastProfile=1 Version=2

[Profile0] Name=default-release IsRelative=1 Path=Profiles/lps6ng9b.default-release

[Profile1] Name=default IsRelative=1 Path=Profiles/d7cjj4nv.default

[Profile2] Name=Nas-Rob IsRelative=0 Path=H:\\Thunderbird profiles\\Rob\\Profiles Default=1

[Install746F856C10C5FA7C] Default=H:\\Thunderbird profiles\\Rob\\Profiles Locked=1

If I run Tbird from the command line to show the profile manager ("d:\Program Files\Mozilla Thunderbird\thunderbird.exe" -ProfileManager), it presents 3 profiles: default-release, default and Nas-Rob. If I select default-release, it brings up Tbird but shows only one of my accounts. If I select default, it requests information to setup an account. If I select Nas-Rob, I get the error that Tbird is already running and the old Tbird process must be closed. If I select “close” the error window closes briefly, and then the same window appears again. I have to cancel to get out of the loop.

I want to use profile2, called Nas-Rob. This is what I used, without a problem for years, prior to the OS reinstallation.

1. Rebooting makes no difference. 2. I’ve confirmed Tbird is not running, using task manager. 3. I have searched the c:, d: and h: drives and deleted all parent.lock files, except those unrelated to Tbird or Firefox. None of this solved the problem. 4. When I try to run "D:\Program Files\Mozilla Thunderbird\thunderbird.exe" -profile "H:\Thunderbird profiles\Rob\Profiles" I get an error that Windows cannot find ‘D:\Program.” In other words, it ignores the double-quotations marks and stops at the first space. So, I don’t seem to be able to run Tbird with run prompts. 5. I tried running the profile from the command prompt. I changed to the d: drive then changed the folder to Program Files\Mozilla Thunderbird. I than ran thunderbird.exe -profile "H:\Thunderbird profiles\Rob\Profiles". This opened up Tbird with all of the email, addresses, etc. associated with the Nas-Rob profile. In other words, this was successful. 6. After exiting Tbird with the profile (#5) and confirming there was no Tbird process running, I ran "D:\Program Files\Mozilla Thunderbird\thunderbird.exe" -profilemanager. This gave me the three profiles described above. As before, when I selected Nas-Rob and clicked to start Tbird, I got the error that Tbird is already running, but is not responding. Indeed, it was running: Tbird started up to run the profile manager. If I selected the default-release profile, instead, Tbird proceeded to open that profile normally. 7. After #6, I again tried running #5. The Nas-Rob profile opened and seems normal. 8. If I change the target for the Tbird desktop icon to "D:\Program Files\Mozilla Thunderbird\thunderbird.exe" -profile "H:\Thunderbird profiles\Rob\Profiles" then it opens the Nas-Rob profile appropriately.

This suggests to me some problem with the profile manager. I assume the profile manager is part of Tbird’s startup process, so if it bombs out when connecting to the Nas-Rob profile then all of Tbird crashes. I haven’t had this problem in the past.

My solution is to specify that the Tbird desktop icon has a target of "D:\Program Files\Mozilla Thunderbird\thunderbird.exe" -Profile "H:\Thunderbird profiles\Rob\Profiles". This bypasses the profile manager. This isn’t my preferred solution, since in the past various updates to Tbird have replaced my icon and its target location with a new one, so I’ll need to remember to edit the target field for the icon to add the profile path.

This seems to be a glitch in Tbird. How to we bring this to the attention of the appropriate persons? I’ve spent many hours trying to diagnose the problem and fix it or come up with a workaround. Others shouldn’t have to do so.
